sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Bothell?
sections.html:
Selling a house in Bothell means selling in a growing Eastside suburb of 52,199 people (Census Bureau estimate, July 1, 2025) that sits in two counties at once. The city lies along the Sammamish River near the northeast end of Lake Washington, and its limits cross from King County into Snohomish County. Owners can list with an agent, sell on their own, or take a cash offer.

The first homestead claims came in 1870, and David Bothell and his family platted the town in 1888. Bothell incorporated in 1909, lived on logging and farming at first, and became a bedroom community for Seattle commuters in the mid-20th century. Interstate 405 now links it to the rest of the Eastside, and downtown has been redeveloped since the 2010s with denser housing.

sections.h2: Which county handles a Bothell sale, King or Snohomish?
sections.html:
The county where the parcel sits handles it. Bothell is one of six Washington cities that span more than one county, and the line follows Northeast 205th Street, which becomes 244th Street Southwest. Many north-south streets change numbers when they cross it. The city annexed Canyon Park in 1992, and that move carried the limits into Snohomish County.

Look at the property tax statement to see which county bills the house. The Department of Revenue says excise tax is paid to the county treasurer in the county where the property is located, so the affidavit and payment go to King County or Snohomish County, not both. The split also touches utilities you will transfer at closing.

  • Electricity comes from Puget Sound Energy on the King County side and from the Snohomish County Public Utility District on the Snohomish side, while Puget Sound Energy supplies natural gas across the city.
  • Four water districts serve the city: Alderwood, Bothell, Northshore and Woodinville.
  • The city contracts with Recology for curbside garbage, recycling and yard waste.

sections.h2: What drives buyer demand in Bothell?
sections.html:
Jobs drive it. Since the 1980s the Canyon Park and North Creek business districts have turned Bothell into a regional employment center, and the city has the second-largest biotechnology hub in Washington, with 61 companies and about 4,000 employees. Pfizer's Seagen, AGC Biologics and Fujifilm Sonosite are among the names there. The University of Washington Bothell and Cascadia College share a campus east of downtown, with about 6,000 students at the university as of 2019.

A 2022 city study found that 29 percent of residents who commute travel to Seattle, 14 percent to Bellevue, 12 percent to Redmond and 8 percent to Kirkland, and that 26 percent work from home. Highway access matters to those buyers: Interstate 405 meets State Route 522 here, and State Routes 524 and 527 serve the north. The Canyon Park Park and Ride and the Swift Green Line run to Lynnwood, Mill Creek and Everett.

sections.h2: Which Bothell neighborhoods and schools should a listing mention?
sections.html:
Bothell's comprehensive plan sorts the city into planning subareas, and about 41 percent of its land is zoned for single-family homes.

  • Downtown Bothell lies north of the Sammamish River between Westhill and Interstate 405.
  • Canyon Park and North Creek hold the office parks, labs and warehouses.
  • Maywood and Beckstrom Hill sit north of downtown, east of the Bothell-Everett Highway.
  • Waynita, Simonds and Norway Hill cover the neighborhoods south of the river and west of the freeway.
  • Brickyard Road and Queensgate occupy the southeast corner.

The Northshore School District serves Bothell and runs 35 schools, 12 of them inside the city. Bothell High School occupies a West Hill campus completed in 1953 and renovated in 2008, and Inglemoor and North Creek high schools also draw Bothell students. The city's hills include slopes south of the Sammamish River that are prone to landslides, and wetlands and creeks run through town, so ask the city whether a lot touches a critical area.

sections.h2: What permits and city rules matter if you sell a Bothell house?
sections.html:
The Permit Center takes permit and land use applications online only, through MyBuildingPermit.com, and answers questions at 425-806-6400 or permits@bothellwa.gov. New zoning rules took effect on January 1, 2025 under BMC 12.14, and the city's CobMap tool shows a parcel's zoning and environmental layers. A buyer planning to add a unit or split a lot should check that map first.

  • Cutting a tree on a lot under 20,000 square feet generally needs no permit if there are no wetlands, streams, steep slopes over 40 percent or shoreline designation.
  • Construction noise is limited to 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Saturdays.
  • If your home's final inspection was more than 90 days ago, the city may not have the plans on file.

Ask the Permit Center whether the house has any open permits, and whether a rental or accessory unit is allowed on the lot, before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: What does a Bothell seller owe at closing?
sections.html:
The seller owes real estate excise tax. RCW 82.45.060 sets four state bands that run from 1.1 percent at the bottom to 3 percent at the top, and the current break points are $525,000, $1,525,000 and $3,025,000. At the Census median value of $925,100, the state portion is $10,896: $5,775 on the first $525,000 plus 1.28 percent of the remaining $400,100. The local portion is added on top, and RCW 82.46.010 lets cities and counties impose local layers of up to 0.25 percent and an additional layer of up to 0.5 percent.

RCW 82.45.080 makes the tax the seller's obligation. Payment is due at the time of sale, and RCW 82.45.100 adds interest after one month plus penalties that climb to 20 percent at three months. Because the buyer is personally liable if the sale is not recorded, title companies normally collect the tax at closing. Ask the closing agent for the exact total for your parcel.

sections.h2: When are property taxes due on a Bothell house?
sections.html:
Washington law makes first-half taxes due April 30 and second-half taxes due October 31. Snohomish County mails statements in mid-February and warns that mail processing can run until May 15 or November 15 during heavy volume. It also offers an interest and penalty waiver after the death of a taxpayer and tax reductions for seniors and disabled owners, which the Assessor's Office at 425-388-3540 can explain. For a King County parcel, call the county's Treasury Operations to confirm the amount before you sell.

Residential property with four or fewer units carries nine percent annual interest on late tax under RCW 84.56.020. Check that no balance is delinquent before you list.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a Bothell house quickly?
sections.html:
With prices this high, a few weeks of carrying costs add up, so many owners compare routes before choosing.

  • List with an agent and prepare the house for the spring market.
  • Sell without an agent and manage the disclosure and the paperwork yourself.
  • Request a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house as-is, which fits an inherited property, a house with deferred repairs or a move with a firm deadline.

Collect the last tax statement, utility accounts and any permit records first, since each speeds up a contract.

faqs.q: Which county do I deal with if my Bothell house is near the county line?
faqs.a: Deal with the county that bills the property tax on that parcel. Excise tax is paid to the treasurer of the county where the property is located, and the tax statement names it.

faqs.q: How much is the state excise tax on a $925,100 Bothell sale?
faqs.a: The state portion is about $10,896. That is 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 and 1.28 percent on the next $400,100, and the local portion is added on top.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Bothell?
faqs.a: April 30 for the first half and October 31 for the second half, in both King and Snohomish counties. Taxes under $50 are due in full on April 30.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to cut a tree before I sell my Bothell house?
faqs.a: Usually not on a lot under 20,000 square feet with no wetlands, streams, steep slopes over 40 percent or shoreline designation. Contact a city planner at planning@bothellwa.gov if you are unsure.

faqs.q: Who supplies electricity and water to Bothell homes?
faqs.a: It depends on the side of the county line and the neighborhood. Puget Sound Energy or the Snohomish County PUD supplies power, and one of four water districts supplies water, so confirm both before you schedule final readings.
